instruction:
Use Abaqus/CAE via the Command Line Interface (CLI) to perform a static tensile analysis of a thin rectangular shell plate with a central circular hole (Variant A). Use the N-mm-MPa unit system.

Part:
Create a 3D Deformable Shell planar part. Sketch a rectangle from (0, 0) to (160, 80) in the X-Y plane. Sketch a circular hole at the plate center (X = 80, Y = 40) with a diameter of 16 mm.

Property:
Create a material named Steel. Set Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Homogeneous Shell Section with thickness = 1.2 mm and 5 integration points. Assign the shell section to the whole plate.

Assembly:
Create one dependent instance of the plate.

Step:
Create a Static, General step named Step-Tension-A. Use small-displacement analysis with nonlinear geometry off.

Boundary Conditions:
Apply U3 = 0 to all plate nodes to keep the shell in the X-Y plane. At the bottom-left corner node (X = 0, Y = 0), apply U1 = U2 = 0. At the bottom-right corner node (X = 160, Y = 0), apply U2 = 0 only.

Loading:
Represent the tensile edge load of 12 N/mm on the left and right vertical edges using equivalent nodal forces after meshing. On the X = 0 edge, apply nodal forces in the negative X direction. On the X = 160 edge, apply nodal forces in the positive X direction. For each loaded edge node, calculate the nodal force as 12 N/mm multiplied by that node's tributary edge length.

Mesh:
Apply a global seed size of 10 mm. Seed the circular hole edge with a size of 4 mm. Use S4R shell elements and generate the mesh.

Job:
Create a job named Job-Hole-A and submit it for solving. Wait for the analysis to complete successfully.

Visualization:
Review the von Mises stress field. Record the maximum von Mises stress and whether it occurs near the circular hole.

Save:
Save the model database to C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-Hole-A.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-Hole-A.odb.
